children: New Delhi, Oct. 12 -- Avenue Supermarts share price declined more than 4% in morning trade on the BSE on Monday, 12 October, after the company reported its September quarter (Q2FY27) results. DMart share price opened at Rs.3,405 against its previous close of Rs.3,520 and dropped 4.4% to hit a 52-week low of Rs.3,366.

Shares of Radhakishan Damani-led Avenue Supermarts declined on Monday after the company reported a modest 8.5% year-on-year (YoY) rise in its Q2FY27 consolidated net profit to Rs.742.98 crore. Total income rose almost 18% YoY to Rs.19,657.50 crore.
Margins declined during the quarter as expenses increased faster than revenue.

Consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 14.7% YoY to Rs.1,393 crore in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA margin contracted to 7.1% from 7.3% in the year-ago quarter. Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) margin also declined to 3.8% from 4.1%.

The stock looks set to extend losses for the third consecutive session. Year-to-date, DMart shares are down 9% compared to a 15% fall in the equity benchmark Sensex. However, on a shorter timeframe of six months, the stock's fall is bigger at 23%, compared to a 7% loss in the Sensex.
